subsystems.name: Entangled photon source
subsystems.role: generates pairs of photons whose quantum states are correlated, the resource consumed by teleportation.
parts: nonlinear crystal for spontaneous parametric down-conversion

subsystems.name: Satellite optical terminal
subsystems.role: transmits and receives single photons through the atmosphere with extreme pointing accuracy.

subsystems.name: Satellite bus
subsystems.role: keeps the payload powered, thermally stable and precisely oriented.

subsystems.name: Ground stations
subsystems.role: receive photons, perform Bell-state measurements and apply corrections.

subsystems.name: Classical communication link
subsystems.role: carries the Bell measurement outcome (two classical bits per teleportation) needed to reconstruct the state; without it no teleportation occurs.

subsystems.name: Quantum memory or repeater (for scaling)
subsystems.role: stores quantum states and extends entanglement over distances beyond direct line of sight.

buildSteps.title: Design the payload
buildSteps.detail: Choose an entangled photon source and an optical terminal that can point and track ground stations while in orbit.

buildSteps.title: Build and test the satellite
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the source, telescope and detectors, then subject the payload to vacuum, vibration and thermal-vacuum testing.

buildSteps.title: Launch and orbit
buildSteps.detail: Place the satellite in low Earth orbit or geostationary orbit, depending on the required link distance and coverage.

buildSteps.title: Prepare ground stations
buildSteps.detail: Upgrade telescopes with single-photon detectors, adaptive optics and precise timing to receive and measure individual photons.

buildSteps.title: Establish entanglement
buildSteps.detail: The satellite generates entangled photon pairs and sends one photon to each of two ground stations, or one to a station and one to another satellite.

buildSteps.title: Perform Bell-state measurement
buildSteps.detail: At one station, a joint measurement is made on the received photon and the quantum state to be teleported, collapsing the entanglement.

buildSteps.title: Send the classical result
buildSteps.detail: The measurement outcome is transmitted over a classical channel to the receiving station; this step is limited by the speed of light.

buildSteps.title: Reconstruct the state
buildSteps.detail: The receiving station applies a unitary transformation based on the classical bits to recover the teleported quantum state.

buildSteps.title: Scale to a network
buildSteps.detail: Add quantum memories and repeaters to link multiple satellites and ground stations, enabling teleportation over global distances.

prerequisites.why: the essential resource for teleportation; demonstrated in labs and on satellites.
needed to send, receive and measure individual photons through the atmosphere.
required to store and synchronize quantum states for repeaters; current memories are inefficient and short-lived.
necessary to extend entanglement beyond direct line of sight and to build a scalable network.
laser communication satellites already achieve the required accuracy.
teleportation always requires a classical channel to transmit the measurement result.

pathway.milestone: ground-to-satellite quantum teleportation and entanglement distribution demonstrated over distances greater than 1000 km (e.g. the Micius satellite, 2017)
pathway.unlocks: proof that fragile quantum states can survive a satellite link.

pathway.milestone: satellite-based quantum key distribution and inter-satellite entanglement links
pathway.unlocks: secure global key exchange and a foundation for a quantum network.

pathway.milestone: quantum repeaters with memories that extend entanglement between distant ground stations
pathway.unlocks: teleportation over intercontinental distances without a direct line of sight.

pathway.milestone: a constellation of quantum satellites forming a global quantum internet
pathway.unlocks: secure communication, distributed quantum sensing and networked quantum computing.
